text: Setting choice: Forgotten Realms, a small invented realm in the Border Kingdoms (south of the Lake of Steam), 1491 DR. The Border Kingdoms are a patchwork of tiny realms that rise and fall, so a new kingdom fits canon.
Lines: none requested. The player is 18+ and mature themes are fine; handle them with craft, not gratuitously. The X-card (typing X) still skips anything immediately.
Veil / table preference: the player must not be shown DM-only information (plot goals, NPC intentions, secrets). See the dm-secrecy block.

Table setup: solo player with one PC; grimdark tone; RoboDM rolls all dice; strict RAW with rules_audit=always; house rules: no encumbrance, unlimited ammo after first purchase, no food/water rules; OOC: prefix means out-of-character talk.

PC concept: Chadickith, a 7 ft, 318 lb Dodrud: a homebrew woolly-mammoth variant of the Loxodon (GGR), purely cosmetic with no rules changes. Tortoiseshell coat of lion-tan and bistre-brown fur. Egotistical know-it-all who gets humbled often. Starts at level 3, standard array, all sourcebooks allowed.
Chadickith backstory: as a child his village was wiped out by a blood-raged roc; he was rescued and raised by a fire giant.
House rule: firearms (DMG optional) are for Artificers only.
Ruling: the optional feats rule is ON (feats may replace Ability Score Improvements). Great Weapon Fighting is only available to Chadickith via Fighting Initiate (TCE) at an ASI level (4+).
Ruling: a Loxodon trunk may hold or carry an object, including a stowed weapon, but can never wield, attack with, load or throw a weapon (GGR is silent; DM ruling).

Ruling: Chadickith starts with a hand crossbow instead of his class's handaxes and javelins, a one-time DM exception to starting equipment. His starting bolts count as his first purchase, so bolts are unlimited.
Chadickith took Primal Knowledge (TCE) at level 3 for Nature. He plans Fighting Initiate (Great Weapon Fighting) at level 4.

Backstory canon (player): Okton developed a ritual that uses his own (infected) blood to create hunters of 'our order'. Chadickith belongs to this order. Whether he has undergone the ritual is unconfirmed.

DM decisions (secret): keep the Heartcoal = Yaga-Shura's burned-out heart (Bhaalspawn) origin. Chadickith does NOT know Okton forged the Crown of Ash. Approved homebrew story mechanics (never shown as rules to the player): roc beacon (a death within 30 ft of the loose coal lets the roc fix its location, arriving in 1d4 days); Ashblood exposure DC 10 WIS save; trying to break the coal deals 2d6 fire. Session 1 opening: scene A 'The King Burns on Highharvestide' (backup: scene B 'The Night Cart'). Calendar: the king died 26 Eleint 1491 DR; session 1 opens on Highharvestide.

Chadickith is 76 years old (rolled 1d21+59). He was 8 when the roc destroyed Hadrun, so the attack happened in 1423 DR. His parents were Berov (father) and Radanya (mother), both killed in the attack. Okton has raised him for 68 years.
Okton's hunter order is named the Order of the Banked Fire; members are called 'the Banked'. Chadickith belongs to the order but has NOT undergone Okton's blood ritual (the Quenching).

Ruling: Okton's blood ritual is how a character gains the Blood Hunter class (Critical Role Blood Hunter on D&D Beyond, 2020). It is allowed as a class, but in-story only through the Quenching. Its rules are NOT in the local 5etools data and D&D Beyond is unreachable from this environment, so check details (multiclass prerequisites etc.) against the player's copy before applying.

Player-supplied Blood Hunter reference (OOC): https://www.scribd.com/document/820591774/Critical-Role-Blood-Hunter . Consult it, or ask the player to paste the relevant parts, when the Quenching or Blood Hunter levels come up.

Session 1: Chadickith now knows the ember is the Heartcoal from the Crown of Ash, that it feeds the 'gladness' infection of the roc and Okton, and that it was stolen from Ivoard's pillow. He does NOT know Okton set it into the crown, its Yaga-Shura origin, or the Glad Choir. Isine (Oselle's household servant) is stable at the Watch triage tent with Wilash guarding. The steward, Lorard's quartermaster and Kitwin saw Chadickith with her; the coal is in a cold-iron box in Okton's forge.

Session 1: a hooded Pyrewarden woman at the Blind Barrel left Chadickith a grey burial-notice note: the knife that cut Isine 'was kept in the Pyrehouse', 'not every warden is glad of it', meet at the Ashward almshouse at tomorrow's dusk bell, and tell no one in a red collar. DM: the writer is a sincere junior Warden unsettled by the Glad Choir (intended as an ally, possibly watched or a trap if the DM wants to complicate). Unresolved.

Session 1: Garford Whitlock, a hired watcher, tailed Chadickith from the Blind Barrel for Lorard's quartermaster. He saw the Pyrewarden leave the note and will report it unless stopped. He claims the Lady Oselle's steward has two men watching Okton's forge. Chadickith grappled him with his trunk.

Ruling: a Loxodon trunk can lift only 5 x STR pounds (75 lb for Chadickith), so it cannot hoist a grown man off the ground; it can grapple, push and pull him. Earlier narration of lifting Garford was corrected: his boots stay on the stones. A slam is an unarmed strike (trunk, +4, 3 bludgeoning); knocking out needs the target reduced to 0 HP with a melee attack (PHB).

Session 1: Jorson, a plain-coated wiry man with Oselle's silver key pin, offered on the Lady's behalf: a private audience at the Ember Keep at dawn bell, 200 gp, a safe-conduct and the Keep's infirmary for Isine, in exchange for seeing what the old woman carried. Chadickith's Insight read him as sincere about the offer but ignorant of what is at stake; he is armed (blade at the small of his back) despite showing empty hands. Answer wanted by dawn.

Session 1: Chadickith let Jorson (Oselle's household) take the unconscious Garford Whitlock, saying 'you can take him or the copper vat can take him.' Oselle's men (three at least, two more hidden in the lane) carried Garford away, claiming the Watch's drunk-tank. Jorson left a silver key on a barrel lid (Ember Keep gate token, answer wanted by dawn). Lorard's quartermaster Fenwin Thatcher will notice Garford never reported back.

Session 1: Chadickith asked Okton directly whether he made the Crown of Ash. Okton admitted it: he forged the cold-iron band for Ivoard Hask in 1453 DR and set the Heartcoal himself, recognised it, and that is when the gladness began in him. Chadickith now KNOWS Okton forged the crown and set the coal. He still does NOT know the coal's Yaga-Shura origin, Okton's desertion, the Glad Choir, or what the Quenching costs.

Session 1: Okton told Chadickith that fire, hammer and pyre cannot break the Heartcoal; it can be undone only in a fire giant's forge fed with a fire giant's own blood, which means Okton, and he fears it may cost him himself. Chadickith does NOT know that destroying the coal would also end the Banked's gift, kill the roc, and likely kill Kitwin.

Junie, a ragged Ashward girl of about nine, told Chadickith that at night covered carts go into the almshouse dead-house and the sisters are forbidden to look. Chadickith told her the story of the roc attack and Okton.

Session 1: Warden Kaselle Redfern (late 20s, cropped dark hair, scar along left jaw, smells only of lye/ash/lavender) met Chadickith at the Ashward almshouse. She named Brother Peret, a lay-brother of the Pyrehouse's inner circle ('the Choir'), as the knife-bearer who killed at Isine; says covered carts bring Ashward dead to the dead-house nightly (19 counted in three months, all with the same smile). She fears the Watch is sold and the High Pyrewarden would hang her. Offers to show Chadickith the dead-house cellar when the midnight cart arrives. Chadickith's Insight failed, so he cannot tell if she is sincere (she is).

Session 1, almshouse dead-house: Chadickith hid in the coffin racks and saw Brother Peret and two Choir brothers bring a smiling dead man (50s, Ashward pauper) at midnight. A narrow closed stab wound under the ribs showed the man was killed, not plague dead. The Choir smelled strongly of hot iron and copper and the cellar warmed. Peret hummed a hymn and told the dead man to 'go gladly'. Kaselle is hiding behind the shroud-stacks.

Session 1, dead-house overheard: Choir brothers speak of 'Coldwell' (High Pyrewarden) being angry that the knife missed and the servant lives; Peret believes the giant's boy (Chadickith) carried her away and that 'the smith has the coal'. Peret places a grey ash wafer on each dead man's tongue; it flares orange and the room warms. A brother noticed the shroud-stacks shift (Kaselle's Stealth 8 vs his Perception 9) and is walking over with a lantern.

Ruling: Chadickith's trunk trumpet blast is free, noise only (no mechanical effect); a shout in Giant is ordinary speech. The failed grapple (13 vs 15) stands; he rolled it before raging, so no advantage. Rage persists only if he attacks or takes damage each turn; his grapple attempt counted as an attack on round 1.

Session 1: Chadickith knocked Peret unconscious (stable, 0 HP) in the almshouse dead-house. Both Choir brothers froze and then surrendered under Chadickith's threats. Okton broke through the ramp door at the end. Okton visibly reacted to the smell of hot iron (a flicker of the gladness). Prisoners: Peret (unconscious), two Choir brothers. Warden Kaselle unharmed. One Fire Strike use left. Rage used 1 of 3.

Ruling: Intimidation can sway NPC morale or behavior as DM fiat; RAW gives no compulsion or morale rule. It never removes an NPC's reaction, forces an action, or imposes a condition. Shouts are free speech; at most one Intimidation check per round, decided with a stated DC and outcome (hesitate/back away) before rolling. The round-2 shout did not cause Peret to flee (he had already decided to); it only affected what the cultists did afterward.

Session 1 interrogation (Intimidation 16): Brothers Vesan (tall) and Wyn (shorter) of the Choir said: the grey wafers are grains of 'the Last Ember' (pyre-ash and dust of the Heartcoal) kept in the Pyrehouse crypt by High Pyrewarden Coldwell; the Choir ends the lives of dying Ashward paupers who 'ask to go gladly' with a narrow blade, the wafer, and a hymn, claiming mercy; about forty-one since the Quiet Year (Flamerule 1490). Coldwell says the Ember will kindle for Kitwin at the Great Pyre tomorrow night 'coal or none', using the grains and the Choir's song. Vesan claimed Kitwin blesses it; Wyn blurted that Kitwin does NOT know and 'must never know'. Okton said the wafer holds dust of the Heartcoal and he did not know they had taken dust. Chadickith's Insight failed (5) so he cannot tell lies from truth beyond that contradiction.

Session 1 deeper interrogation (Intimidation 17): the Choir is eleven in the inner circle (3 captured, 8 free incl. Sister Ilsa the cantor and Brother Garn). The casket of grains, 'the Last Ember', is in an iron box in the Pyrehouse crypt below the sanctum; Coldwell wears the key. A bricked 'plague road' tunnel behind the lye barrels in this dead-house cellar runs to the crypt; Peret carries the key to its iron gate. Tomorrow night at the second bell after dusk, at the Great Pyre, Kitwin will kneel; if the coal does not kindle, Coldwell will press grains into the crown's socket and the Choir will sing it alight so Kitwin believes the Ember chose him. Chadickith's Insight (10) could not confirm every detail, but the brothers appear terrified.

Session 1: Chadickith (with Kaselle's help) found Peret's iron plague-road gate key on a neck cord, a tin of three ash wafers, a narrow stiletto, and a folded list of six Ashward names (each with a date and a mark; two marked done). Chadickith told Okton he is turning Peret in to the Collarhouse, asking Okton to keep Kaselle safe and handle the two brothers; Okton objects (Halda sells everyone) but will keep Kaselle and the brothers alive and bound at the forge.

Session 1: Chadickith handed unconscious Peret to Watch-Captain Halda at the Collarhouse in the small hours, saying only that Peret was the knife-man who cut the servant, caught at the almshouse dead-house after a warden's tip (Kaselle unnamed). A rooftop watcher (Choir lookout) tailed him part of the way. Halda will hold Peret but warns High Pyrewarden Coldwell will demand him by sunup and she can only hold him until the dusk bell.

Who-knows-what LEDGER (end of the dead-house night): HALDA knows: Chadickith saved Isine; he may hold something Isine gave him (she believes he passed it off); Peret is the knife-man (Chadickith said so, source 'a warden' unnamed); Peret is in her cells. She does NOT know: the Heartcoal, Okton's secrets, the Choir, Kaselle, the plague road. ORSELLE'S SIDE (Oselle, steward, Jorson, Garford now in their hands): know Chadickith carried Isine and likely holds what she carried (they suspect, not know); Jorson suspects his lie; Garford (captive) saw the Pyrewarden note passed at the Blind Barrel. They do NOT know about the Choir, dead-house, Okton's confession. LORARD'S SIDE (Thatcher): knows Chadickith was with Isine and was tailed; lost his watcher Garford; knows nothing of the dead-house. THE CHOIR/COLDWELL: know Isine lived, the 'giant's boy' carried her, suspect 'the smith has the coal'; a lookout saw Chadickith carry Peret to the Collarhouse; they know Peret's team failed but not by whom or how. KITWIN: does not know the Choir kills; sat with Isine's cot; sincere. KASELLE: knows Chadickith, Okton, the Choir's methods, that Peret is captured. OKTON: knows everything Chadickith knows plus the coal's history.

Session 1: Chadickith hid Peret's tin of three ash wafers in a hollow behind the smoke-hood in the forge's roof-beams, wrapped in an oiled rag, away from the Heartcoal's slab under the hearth. Kaselle was sent outside during the hiding and does not know where it is. Okton asked that the wafers stay out of his reach.

Session 1: Isine Kettle (king's cupbearer, hurt but recovering at the Watch triage tent, Wilash guarding) told Chadickith: Ivoard Hask stopped the executions in Flamerule 1490 because the coal was burning him from the inside and he tried to starve it; his true last words were 'Break it. Not them, none of them. Break it.' and he did NOT name Kitwin his heir. Coldwell invented the naming. She stole the coal because the king begged her to; she believes every heir will use it. She fears Kitwin because the coal glows for him and he is too kind to see what it does.

Session 1, day 2 afternoon: Halda agrees to issue a Saltgate pass for Isine (with Wilash as escort), but only to leave at the dusk bell rotation when the Pyre crowds fill the streets and Coldwell's watchers are thinner; Chadickith's Persuasion (5) failed to get it sooner. She asks him to work her rope line at the Great Pyre tonight (double pay). Peret, awake in the cells, has only hummed hymns and asked for 'the loxodon'.

Session 1, day 2 late afternoon: Chadickith handed Halda's Saltgate pass to Isine herself (not Wilash), with the proviso she may give it up later. Isine is ready to leave at the dusk bell rotation with Wilash as escort. At the forge Chadickith briefed Okton; Okton proposed using the plague road during the Pyre rite while most of the Choir sing at the Great Pyre, since a giant cannot fit the tunnel himself.

Session 1: Chadickith chose to honor Halda's rope-line job at the north rail of the Great Pyre rather than raid the crypt during the rite. Okton agreed. Signal agreed: a loxodon trumpet blast means Okton should come at once. Okton will watch from the Pyre Square's edge; Kaselle stays at the forge with the brothers. The plague-road gate key stays with Chadickith.

Session 1, Great Pyre rite (second bell after dusk): Coldwell set the Crown of Ash on Kneeling Kitwin with grey grains packed into the socket; the grains glowed faintly then guttered. The Choir shifted its hymn and led a smiling old Ashward volunteer onto the dais; Brother Garn drew a narrow blade behind the old man and Kitwin as Chadickith watched from the north rail. Chadickith has not yet acted.

Session 1, Great Pyre rite: Garn killed the smiling old volunteer on the dais while Kitwin held his hand; the grains in the Crown of Ash flared and the crown kindled orange. The crowd roared that the Ember had chosen Kitwin; Lorard's soldiers and Oselle's guard bristled; the rope line surged. Chadickith watched without acting and resisted the Ashblood warmth (WIS save 14 vs DC 10). Kitwin looked down at the blade and wept and smiled at once. Halda's Watch is on edge.
Lorard will not help disperse the crowd until Kitwin's crowning is publicly challenged; he demanded Chadickith step aside. Crowd ignored Chadickith's order to disperse.
Roc veered off from Garn and Kitwin on the dais when it stooped, striking the pyre instead; Chadickith saw it. Chadickith abandoned Kitwin after a failed grab (nat 1).
Chadickith captured Brother Garn (bound, gagged) after Okton knocked him out; Kitwin was spirited toward the Pyrehouse lane by Sister Ilsa and another Choir member.

Ruling: Chadickith's rage ended at the end of his round-4 turn (no attack, no damage taken since); the Dash back to the guildhall was unraged. 1 of 3 rages used since the long rest. Garn is stable at 0 HP (nonlethal KO) and wakes at 1 HP after 3 hours; rope bind breaks on a STR 17 burst, gag is a ruling only for spells with verbal components.

Lorard's field kit outside Kharun: crossbow companies plus four light bolt-throwers (ballistae) on carts; none inside the walls. The Ember Keep roof has two bolt-throwers under Oselle's grey halberds. Lorard says the Gallowsbird is the late king's own Sky Gallows bird and he has never seen it turn on its own city.

Garn answered under questioning (gag removed): he does NOT control the roc; he raised his hands only to bless the crowd. He believes the bird 'knows the chosen' and spared Kitwin because the Hearth chose him. DM truth: the roc is Glad (Ashblood), drawn to the loose Heartcoal and kin-sensing Kitwin (Kindled); Garn does not know why it veered.

Garn (bound, 1 HP) said Kitwin was taken down to the Pyrehouse sanctum, to the crypt where the Last Ember (casket of grains) waits and the crown must be 'kept warm' until the dawn bell; Coldwell will meet them. He invited Chadickith to follow.

Chadickith broke Garn's leg and threw him bound out the guildhall door as bait; the roc took him in the open. Lorard and the surgeon witnessed it; Lorard now has no prisoner and a harder opinion of Chadickith.

Halda refused to open the Saltgate to Lorard's carts (Okton's persuasion failed, 5 vs DC 12). She will allow only the bolt-throwers' crews through the wicket on foot with the engines broken down, which takes about two hours. The roc keeps raking the square meanwhile.

Chadickith organized the evacuation of the Great Pyre square with Lorard's shield-men and the Watch (Intimidation 21 vs DC 12, advantage): crowds funneled into guildhalls, cellars and the Collarhouse. Many saved, but the roc still killed dozens. Lorard's opinion of Chadickith softened slightly. The engine crews started through the Saltgate wicket after roughly two hours.

PENDING: Chadickith was killed by the Gallowsbird (instant death, RAW-verified by the rules-lawyer) in Round 5 of the roc fight; the player must choose whether to accept the death and roll a new PC, or have the DM rewind before the roc's target roll. Roc 84/248, Okton 108/162 grappled, sergeant 20/22 at ballista 3.

THE QUENCHING: Okton performed the blood rite on dying Chadickith (round 6 of the roc fight) after the player chose rescue option 3. Price: forced class change, Barbarian -> Blood Hunter (details to come from the player's Scribd reference). Chadickith woke at 1 HP, prone. DM secret: every Banked is Touched by Ashblood from the moment of quenching, tempered toward fury.

Chadickith is now Blood Hunter 3 (Alternate, laserllama v2.2) / Order of the Pale Moon, Beast = Giant Owl (Hybrid Form keeps the trunk as a tail). Rites: Binding, Revelation. Fighting Style: Great Weapon Fighting. Occult Lore: Arcana. Perception swapped for Investigation (Feral Senses adds the Rite Die to Perception/Survival). Saves: CON, CHA. Rulings: no Vital Sacrifice that would reduce current HP to 0; Binding can't hold Gargantuan creatures (the roc) unless empowered. Reference notes in Books/alternate-blood-hunter-notes.md.
RESOLVED by DM fudge: Chadickith's second death (R7 massive damage) was rewound to the start of his round-7 turn at the player's request. No further rescues. Roc 84/248, Okton 77/162, sergeant 20/22.

THE GALLOWSBIRD IS DEAD: Okton killed it in round 8 at the Great Pyre after the bolt-throwers, his rocks and his sword wore it down. Okton is at 15/162 HP, near death. Chadickith is at 1 HP. Lorard's sergeant died at the engines; roughly a hundred townsfolk died in the square. Ashblood effects of the roc's death are not yet known to the party.

SECRET: when the Gallowsbird died, newly Quenched Chadickith felt a flash of heat and fury he first mistook for pleasure (Stirring). Okton felt it more strongly and held it down; his eyes caught red and his wrist veins showed grey.

Rulings: (1) the Quenching bargain voided the instant death AND one crit failure (death saves 1/1 instead of RAW 1/2): DM fiat. (2) Nature proficiency came from the Barbarian's Primal Knowledge and was removed with the class change (can be restored as a deliberate concession). (3) Okton's attacks while grappled/restrained by the roc's talons should have had disadvantage; the final blow was re-rolled and still hit.

Dawn, day 3 (after the long rest at Okton's forge): Okton and Chadickith fully rested. Overnight Halda released Peret to Coldwell at the dusk bell as she had warned. At the dawn bell the Pyrehouse bell tolled out of rhythm and a grey smoke column rose from the Pyrehouse; Coldwell is proclaiming Kitwin 'kindled' (Choir sang the crown alight again). Isine and Wilash never left: the Saltgate stayed shut after the roc and they are working the Collarhouse triage tent. Vesan, Wyn and Kaselle remain at the forge.

Dawn, day 3 at the Collarhouse: Halda says the Kharun Watch swore to keep the peace 'until the Coal chooses'; Coldwell says it has chosen Kitwin, which would end the oath and open the gates at noon. Halda privately doubts it and asked Chadickith whether the Ember truly kindled. She let Coldwell take Peret at the dusk bell with a Watch escort. Isine and Wilash are working the triage tent; Isine still has the pass and wants out.

DEADLINE: Chadickith told Halda the Ember never kindled (Persuasion 7 vs DC 11, fail): she believes he believes it but needs proof, not a guard's word. Unless she has proof the Coal did NOT choose Kitwin by noon, she will honour the oath as written, open the gates and let Coldwell's claim stand.

Halda agreed to meet Chadickith and Okton at the forge within the hour, coming alone by the tannery postern. On the way back Chadickith (Perception 13 vs DC 13, Feral Senses) spotted a grey-scarfed Choir lookout tailing him through the lanes.
Chadickith lost the Choir lookout (Survival 21 vs DC 14, advantage) and reached the forge unfollowed. The lookout turned back toward the Pyrehouse; he will report that Chadickith went to the forge.

At the forge Okton refused to touch the tin of ash wafers (a risk he will not take); Chadickith fetched it from the roof beams and showed Halda. Halda recognised the Pyrewarden's grey wafers and said Coldwell can claim they are blessed bread; she asked to question the bound brothers Vesan and Wyn as witnesses.

SECRET OUT: Chadickith had Okton lift the hearth slab and show Halda the real Heartcoal. Halda now knows it is hidden in Okton's forge. She felt its warmth and stepped back; her reaction: the Coal did NOT choose Kitwin, so under her oath she will keep the gates sealed past noon, but she wants the brothers' testimony and demands the coal be covered. Risk: the Choir lookout may report the forge.

Halda questioned Vesan and Wyn at the forge: they swore the Choir pressed grains from the iron casket (the 'Last Ember') into the crown's socket and sang it alight, that Coldwell wears the casket's key and keeps it in the Pyrehouse crypt, and that they were meant to be among the singers. Halda believes them. She wants them sworn before her captains at noon but Okton fears Coldwell will reach them in the Collarhouse.

Agreement: Chadickith will escort Vesan and Wyn to the Collarhouse courtyard at noon to be sworn before Halda's captains; Halda leaves now to gather them without saying why. Okton stays to guard the Heartcoal at the forge. About four and a half hours remain.

Chadickith insisted Okton join the noon escort. Okton agreed, reluctantly: Kaselle stays at the forge to guard the sealed hearth slab (barred door); Chadickith, Okton and the brothers Vesan and Wyn will walk to the Collarhouse courtyard. Risk: the forge is guarded only by Kaselle while they are away; the Choir lookout may have marked it.

Okton explained the Quenching to Chadickith: the rite mixes his own blood, which carries the burn (Ashblood), with the subject's; it makes the rage manageable rather than curing it; the beast shape (giant owl) is chosen by the blood. He pulled Chadickith back from death, which he had never done for someone already dead. He warned that the heat Chadickith felt when the roc died is the rage stirring, and not to feed it. Okton did not mention forging the Crown of Ash.

Okton rebuilt (player approved): level 18 Pale Moon Blood Hunter on top of the fire giant block, PB +6, HP 315, Rite DC 20, Rite Die d10, roc form as a progenitor exception, feats Tough/Sentinel/Great Weapon Master/Alert. DM secret: he kept it sealed in the roc fight because Rites feed the gladness.

Okton admitted to Chadickith that Chadickith is only the SECOND person he has ever quenched. The first was a dying Watch veteran last winter, held nine days and then died in a rage, teeth bared. Okton refined the rite after it. Chadickith is the first to survive. Each Quenching costs Okton 1 max HP and 1 year of life (craft rank 1).

LORE REWORK (player decisions, round 1): Ashblood stays the Heartcoal's overflow, but creatures with class level 3 or lower or CR 1/2 or lower DIE from the overflow, and higher level/CR creatures are INFECTED. Okton found a non-deadly variant (the Quenching) that converts low-level adventurers into Blood Hunters; it is not reliably survivable, but Okton hones it over time and can expand the order. Symptoms: bloodlust and rage, NO joy. Cure: none, only management. Okton: stable and disciplined (no ticking clock). Still to define: exposure trigger, Kitwin, Quenching survival mechanic, stage names.

LORE REWORK (round 2 decisions): Exposure is disease-like: touching the Heartcoal, its blood, or contact with anyone who is or was in contact with the overflow. Kitwin is secretly infected (an anomaly: he should have died as a boy). The Quenching's survival scales by level and above all by WILLINGNESS (willingness matters far more than level; higher level survives better); Okton hones the craft over time. Stages renamed: Stirring (rage you can hold), Frenzied (you lose control in combat), Berserk (the rage never leaves). Open: what happens if the Coal is destroyed; the cost to Okton; the Choir's faith; retcons ('died smiling', Chadickith's 'warmth').

Forge downtime before noon (quiet, no Choir probe): Kaselle described the Pyrehouse for Chadickith and Okton: a walled cemetery, the sanctum above, the crypt below with the Last Ember casket; the plague-road gate opens from the dead-house tunnel. Okton drilled Chadickith on Hybrid Form and holding the rage down. The brothers Vesan and Wyn slept. It is about an hour before noon.

Noon, day 3, Collarhouse courtyard: Halda's six Watch captains stand in a half-ring (named: Yarelle Pike, Marda Ironside, Hesard Rook; three others unnamed). Halda wants Vesan and Wyn sworn before them. The crowd outside is kneeling to Coldwell's smoke; half the Watch is wavering.

Noon, day 3: Halda led the hearing in the Collarhouse courtyard; Vesan and Wyn swore the Choir lit the crown with grains from the Last Ember casket. Halda's persuasion succeeded (22 vs DC 14): her six captains agreed the Coal did NOT choose Kitwin and the Watch keeps the gates sealed, publicly refusing Coldwell's claim. Captain Hesard Rook looked uneasy and left soon after. Halda did not tell the captains about the real Heartcoal. Coldwell will answer.

Okton's read on Lorard: he sides with whoever opens the Saltgate for him without a sack. The Watch refusing Coldwell suits him now, because it clears the eldest son's path. The danger comes when he asks where the real Coal is. Okton warned Chadickith to keep the forge hidden from him.

Lorard's ultimatum (public): open Kharun's gates within ten days of the king's death or he storms the city; about six days remain on the morning of day 3. Everyone remembers the Thornwater Tithe (he hanged every tenth man there), so the threat is believed.

Collarhouse triage tent, noon day 3: Isine reports that of about forty people wounded by the Gallowsbird (blood contact), nineteen died overnight of the burn and seven are raging or restrained (infected). She keeps the rest apart, washes wounds with brine and tells the staff not to touch blood. SECRET: Isine herself is infected (Stirring), an anomaly because she touched the Coal and lived on willingness; she does not know. She noticed the red catch in Chadickith's eyes and the grey veins at his wrists.

Okton explained the Quenching rules in-world on the walk to the tent: three stages (Stirring: hot, held; Frenzied: wild in a fight; Berserk: lost), no cure, a Banked can bleed rage off with a Vital Sacrifice, survival depends mostly on willingness, and each Quenching costs him a hit point and a year.

Chadickith and Okton moved Isine's seven raging Watchmen into the Collarhouse cellar under Halda's order (quarantine, no blood contact). One broke his restraints; Chadickith pinned him (Athletics 21 vs DC 14) without being bitten. Isine refuses to leave: she will keep treating the roc-wounded. Wilash still holds the Saltgate pass.

RULE (player decision): the Quenching on someone LOST IN THE RAGE (Berserk) is a d20 + their level (or CR); 10 or higher converts them, lower and they die. Stirring/Frenzied hosts count as willing (+10). Everyone else uses the standard Quenching check. Okton will still wait for a lucid moment and a clear yes.
